Phase 1 RCA (Understand complete, before repair):

Step 0(a): searched `deterministic readiness floor Acceptance Criteria Testing Verification signed plan_review floor` and listed open/in_progress bugs; only this ticket matched the same symptom directly. Step 0(b): report has no build SHA, so created_at 1788376258971939001 gives floor `3e22693efc9013574f947ad7cd7ff797a8cd39c9`; suspect plan-review files changed afterward. Step 0(c): worktree `tomophobic-floor` is current at `035a50310268c767e6c3d7eca0d46e89a0b8f033` (= origin/main).

Confirmed mechanism: `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py::plan_review_precheck` takes an ordinary (non-escalated) `bug` through the lightweight bug-tier arm. That arm runs `det_floor.run_det_floor`, then keeps only P4 in `det_blocking` and moves every other deterministic block into `det_advisories`. Therefore P1 (`no standard ## Acceptance Criteria checklist`) and P10 (`no Testing/Verification section...`) are observed by the floor but discarded as authoritative blocks before the short-circuit decision. For task siblings, the normal arm keeps those same P1/P10 findings in `det_blocking`, so `run_llm=False` and terminal verdict BLOCK.

Runtime proof: I reconstructed the three pre-rewrite descriptions from `.tickets-tracker/<id>` event history. Direct `run_det_floor(PlanContext(...))` produced P1+P10 blocks for all three descriptions (0 headings, 0 checkboxes). Driving the actual `plan_review_precheck` step produced BLOCK/no-LLM for `545a-4db5-3a64-42d9` and `0d3c-ff25-5317-4d73`, but for bug `fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad` produced `run_llm=True`, `verdict=None`, `det_blocking=[]`, `det_advisory=[P1,P10,P9]`, `bug_tier=True`. That rules out nondeterministic heading parsing, batch mutation, and model sampling; the divergent verdict is the bug-tier downgrade path.

Defect legitimacy: this is a `defect`. `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents Layer 1 as the deterministic floor and names P1 (missing `## Acceptance Criteria`) and P10 (missing testing/verification proof) as sound unambiguous blockers; the signed plan-review attestation is what the claim gate consumes. A signed PASS with P1/P10 present as DET findings violates that deterministic-floor contract and the invariant that a certified plan has objective acceptance/verification criteria.

Attribution: origin is commit `cbc5b2880eb804d1d9c0aa73a791bd04bda827e1` (`03a9-e6d1-4acc-435d`, alias `clerkish-cloggy-cod`) titled `03a9: necessity/no-op probe + lightweight bug review tier (R4, advisory)`. `git log -L` shows that commit introduced the bug-tier rule "every DET finding is downgraded to advisory (det_blocking=[])"; later commits only narrowed the exception to P4 / added escalation. This is the change that made P1/P10 non-authoritative for ordinary bugs, so the close should use `--class=regression --caused-by=clerkish-cloggy-cod`.

Expected post-fix behavior: P1/P10 readiness-floor failures remain blocking for all work-ticket types, including ordinary bug-tier reviews; well-formed bugs still get the substantive lightweight advisory review instead of bare exempt PASS.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The plan-review gate's **deterministic Layer-1 floor** admitted a ticket that violates two of its
own blocking checks, while blocking two sibling tickets of the SAME shape in the same minutes.

## Evidence

Three children of epic `undamaged-murderous-horse` (f79d-0d71-0fd7-439f) were filed by the same
sweep, in the same format: a bare prose finding with **no `##` headings at all and zero
`- [ ]` checkboxes**.

All three were reviewed concurrently at ~11:56-12:02 PDT on 2026-09-02, same store, same build:

| ticket | shape at review | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `refutable-goosebumpy-opossum` (545a-4db5-3a64-42d9) | bare prose, 0 headings, 0 checkboxes | **BLOCK** |
| `misandrous-defaceable-zenaida` (0d3c-ff25-5317-4d73) | bare prose, 0 headings, 0 checkboxes | **BLOCK** |
| `classical-grey-ayeaye` (fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad) | bare prose, 0 headings, 0 checkboxes | **PASS + signed** |

Both BLOCKs cite the floor verbatim:

- "The ticket fails the deterministic readiness floor: no standard `## Acceptance Criteria` checklist."
- "The plan states no verification: no Testing/Verification section and no acceptance criterion names a proving command or verification step."

`classical-grey-ayeaye` satisfies NEITHER condition and was nonetheless signed. Its result carries
`coverage.llm_ran: true` and `source: attested`, so this was a full review, NOT a short-circuit
reuse of an older attestation and not a cached verdict.

Reproduce the shape difference:

    rebar show classical-grey-ayeaye   # 0 headings, 0 checkboxes -> PASS
    rebar show <either sibling>        # same shape at review time -> BLOCK

(The two siblings now show 5 checkboxes because they were rewritten IN RESPONSE to the block;
the store's event history holds their pre-rewrite descriptions.)

## Phase 1 confirmed RCA and repair plan

The CREATE events in `.tickets-tracker/{545a-4db5-3a64-42d9,0d3c-ff25-5317-4d73,fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad}` hold the review-time bare descriptions. Direct runtime calls to `det_floor.run_det_floor(PlanContext(...))` over those exact descriptions all produce P1 and P10 blocking findings. Driving the production workflow precheck over the same three descriptions explains the divergence: task tickets keep P1/P10 in `det_blocking` and return terminal BLOCK, while ordinary bug tickets go through `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py::plan_review_precheck`'s lightweight bug-tier branch, where P1/P10 are moved from `det_blocking` to `det_advisory`; the later LLM tier can then return PASS and sign. The responsible path is the bug-tier DET downgrade in `plan_review_precheck`, not nondeterministic parsing, batching, or model sampling.

Minimal fix: keep the lightweight bug review tier for well-formed ordinary bugs, but preserve P1/P10 readiness-floor failures (and existing P4 description-limit failures) as authoritative DET blocks before any LLM pass. Non-readiness DET findings remain advisory in the bug tier. Documentation is updated only to match the restored contract.

Regression plan:

- Direct-floor unit coverage proves all three exact pre-rewrite descriptions trip P1/P10.
- Production `plan_review_precheck` coverage proves all three exact descriptions short-circuit to BLOCK, including the `classical-grey-ayeaye` bug fixture.
- The same test runs the collection in normal and reversed order to prove order independence.
- Existing well-formed bug-tier tests prove a clean bug still runs the substantive lightweight advisory LLM tier and is not restored to bare exemption.
- Mutation check reintroduces the P1/P10 downgrade and confirms the held-out regression test returns RED.

## Why it matters

1. **A signed attestation is the artifact the claim gate consumes.** A plan admitted without
   acceptance criteria produces a certified claim for work whose completion cannot later be
   verified — the completion verifier reads those criteria. The close then fails for a ticket
   whose plan the gate itself certified as ready, which is where I hit it.
2. **"Deterministic" is the floor's whole selling point.** Layer 1 exists so a structural defect
   is caught identically every time, before any model judgment. If it is order-, batch-, or
   model-dependent, an author cannot tell a real structural gap from a coin flip, and the
   documented revise -> review -> claim loop stops converging.
3. It silently weakens every downstream gate that assumes a reviewed plan has criteria.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: the floor's `## Acceptance Criteria` check and its Testing/Verification check produce
      the SAME verdict for the same description text, independent of concurrency, batching, or
      model sampling. Verified by a test feeding the three descriptions above through the floor
      directly and asserting all three BLOCK, and by driving the production precheck path to prove
      no later LLM path can discard those P1/P10 blocks.
- [ ] AC2: a regression test pins the exact `classical-grey-ayeaye` pre-rewrite description (from
      the store's event history) as a BLOCK case, so this specific admission cannot recur.
- [ ] AC3: the root cause is identified and named — whether the floor is bypassed on some path,
      evaluated non-deterministically, or its result discarded when a later pass returns PASS.
      Verified by the fix citing the responsible code path.
- [ ] AC4 [non-codebase]: if any other signed attestation in the store was minted over a plan
      lacking acceptance criteria, those tickets are listed in a comment so their claims can be
      re-reviewed rather than silently trusted.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py -k "plan_review_bug_floor" -q` — direct-floor and production-precheck regression/determinism tests over the three pre-rewrite descriptions.
- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py tests/unit/test_bug_blast_radius_escalation_ad0d.py tests/unit/workflow/test_det_short_circuit.py -q` — preserves bug-tier, escalation, and DET short-circuit behavior.
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
- `rebar explain plan` remains accurate about what the floor requires.

Keep run_plan_review documentation aligned with P1/P10/P4 blocking behavior for bug-tier reviews.
Regression/determinism tests using the three pre-rewrite descriptions, including the exact classical-grey-ayeaye fixture.
Update bug-tier/escalation expectations so P1/P10 readiness failures remain blocking even without blast-radius escalation.
Update pre-existing bug-tier downgrade coverage to pin non-readiness advisory behavior without contradicting P1/P10 blocking.
Keep light-tier workflow test on a well-formed bug so it still proves the LLM tier runs when readiness checks pass.
Update bug-tier documentation to state that P1/P10 readiness-floor failures still block bugs.
